results.title: Supabase Pricing in 2026: What You'll Actually Pay (with Calculator)
results.snippet:
Supabase costs $0 on the Free plan (500 MB database, 50,000 monthly active users, 5 GB egress, auto-pauses after 1 week idle), and $25/month on the Pro plan, which bundles Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Postgres together. The Pro plan includes a $10/month compute credit that covers one Micro instance, so most early-stage SaaS apps stay at exactly $25/month. A growing SaaS on a Small compute tier with 20 GB storage and 300 GB egress lands around $36/month. Team and Enterprise plans [...] Supabase costs $0 on the Free plan and $25/month on the Pro plan. Pro bundles Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Postgres, and includes a $10 compute credit that covers a Micro instance, so most early-stage SaaS apps stay at exactly $25/month. A growing SaaS with a Small compute tier, 20 GB storage, and 300 GB egress runs about $36/month.

Is Supabase free? [...] Supabase pricing starts at $0 on the Free plan and $25/month on the Pro plan, but the Pro price is a base fee, not a flat rate. On top of it you pay for your compute tier (minus a $10 credit), database storage past 8 GB, and egress past 250 GB. Most articles report "$25 a month" and stop there, so the extra meters first show up on the invoice.

This post lists every Supabase rate, checks it against our Supabase pricing calculator, and works out the monthly bill for four workloads.

results.title: Supabase Pro: 2026 Pricing, Quotas, and Features Guide - Build Your App in 4-8 weeks | Bricks Tech
results.snippet:
The supabase pro plan starts with a straightforward base price of $25 per month. This isn’t a per project fee, but rather an organization level subscription. You upgrade an entire organization to Pro, and all the projects within it get the benefits.

This $25 base fee includes the resources for your first project. If you want to run more projects within the same Pro organization, each additional one costs about $10 per month, assuming it uses the default Micro compute size. [...] Understand Supabase Pro in 2026—$25/mo org billing, $10 compute credit, 100K MAU, 8GB DB, 100GB storage, 250GB egress. See overages, add‑ons, and cost tips. [...] Every paid Supabase plan, including Pro, comes with a $10 per month compute credit. This credit is applied to your database hosting costs. The default database instance on the Pro plan (the “Micro” tier) costs around $10 per month, so this credit covers it completely.

In simple terms, your $25 monthly subscription includes one project running on a Micro database at no extra charge. If you need to scale up to a more powerful database, the $10 credit is simply subtracted from the higher cost.

results.title: Supabase Pricing Page and Costs Explained (2026)
results.snippet:
### Pro

Pro is Supabase's most popular pricing plan. It is the main starting point for companies building production applications.

Image

Source: Supabase.com

At $25/month, the Pro plan supports up to 100,000 monthly active users. It also includes a larger database size (8 GB per project), more storage (100 GB), higher bandwidth consumption (250 GB egress), and daily backups for seven days. Plus, it unlocks email support. [...] Supabase is not costly for small teams or early-stage startups. The Free tier offers generous limits, while the Pro plan starts at $25/month. Costs only increase when your app uses more compute, storage, bandwidth, monthly active users, or paid add-ons.

### Is Supabase cheaper than AWS?

Supabase can be cheaper and easier to budget than AWS because it offers predictable pricing plans. AWS may provide more services, but pricing can be harder to predict across multiple products. [...] The first Supabase project in Pro is included. However, additional projects cost $10/month.

The Pro plan introduces usage-based pricing with overage charges. You can pay as you go for additional usage that exceeds the plan limits.

To keep costs under control, Supabase enables a spend cap by default. You can start small and expand over time without worrying about runaway billing.

You also have the option to switch off the spend cap to enable usage-based scaling beyond Pro's included quota.
